comparativa.lead: Cloud services take your signal, relay it from their servers and charge you for it. Muxlyve does the relaying from your PC: no watermark, no third-party bandwidth and no monthly fee per hour streamed.
comparativa.tableTitle: Cloud vs. local relay, point by point

comparativa.fairness: To be fair: local relaying uses your upload bandwidth once per active platform. If your upload is limited, a cloud service that uploads only once may suit you better. Muxlyve wins when you have upload headroom and don't want a subscription or a watermark.
comparativa.whenCloudTitle: A cloud service suits you if…
whenCloud: Your upload can't handle several platforms at once.
You stream from networks you don't control (events, coworking, hotels).
You need the stream to keep running after you shut your machine down.
You want a web studio, remote guests and cloud recording in one product.
whenLocal: You have enough upload and don't want to pay for someone else's bandwidth.
You don't want a third-party watermark over your content.
You'd rather buy a lifetime license than pay a subscription forever.
You don't want your signal passing through someone else's servers.
You already use OBS, Streamlabs, XSplit, vMix or N.Air and don't want to change your workflow.

faq.a: No. Muxlyve is neither an encoder nor a plugin: it receives the RTMP signal OBS (or Streamlabs, XSplit, vMix, N.Air) already produces and relays it to several platforms at once. You keep the software you already use.

faq.q: Does quality drop when streaming to 4 platforms?
faq.a: No, because Muxlyve doesn't re-encode: it relays the same signal with -c copy and minimal CPU load. What you do need is upload bandwidth for every active destination.

faq.q: How much upload do I need?
faq.a: Roughly your bitrate multiplied by the number of active platforms. At 6,000 kbps across 3 platforms, about 18 Mbps of stable upload.
Yes, by pasting the RTMP key TikTok gives you. Note that TikTok regenerates that key roughly every 2 hours — a limitation of their platform, not Muxlyve.

faq.q: What happens if a platform drops mid-stream?
faq.a: Muxlyve reconnects it automatically without cutting your other destinations, and warns you with a system notification.

faq.q: Is there a one-time payment license?
faq.a: Yes. Alongside the monthly and yearly plans there's a one-time lifetime license.

que-es-muxlyve.title: What is Muxlyve?
que-es-muxlyve.summary: What Muxlyve does and how it differs from a cloud restream service.
que-es-muxlyve.metaDescription: Muxlyve streams your signal to Twitch, Kick, YouTube and TikTok Live at the same time, watermark-free, running on your own computer.
que-es-muxlyve.content:
Muxlyve streams your signal to Twitch, Kick, YouTube and TikTok Live at the same time, watermark-free.

How is it different from a cloud service?

Services like Restream or Castr run on a third-party server: you send them your signal, and they forward it. Muxlyve runs on your own computer — you generate the signal in your streaming software (OBS, Streamlabs, XSplit, vMix, or anything else that speaks RTMP), Muxlyve receives it locally and forwards it to each platform directly. It never passes through a third-party server.

012
highlights: Runs on your own PC, not a third-party server.
Streams to Twitch, Kick, YouTube and TikTok at once.
No watermark, never routed through external servers.

From the same chat, without leaving Twitch's website: timeout (1 min / 10 min / 1 hour) or permanent ban on a message. Moderate without switching windows.

Translate chat messages

In Preferences → Chat, turn on "Translate chat messages" (off by default). When a message arrives in a language different from the app's, Muxlyve shows the translation as a separate line under the original message — it never replaces it.

It uses an unofficial third-party service (Google Translate), so it's best-effort: it may silently fail on a specific message, and the chat keeps working just as well, just without that translation.

grabador-clips.content:
Clip buffer

Muxlyve records into a circular buffer (30s / 1min / 2min) while you stream, so you can save "what just happened" without recording the entire stream.

Turn on the buffer, and save the clip to a configurable folder with one click.

0

Full recording

Besides the buffer, Muxlyve can record the whole stream into a single file, from start to finish. It's independent from the clip buffer — each one is turned on separately, with its own switch, on the main panel.

The destination folder is chosen in Preferences → Clip recorder → "Full recordings folder".

perfiles-destinos.title: Profiles: switch from "Twitch only" to "everything" in one click
perfiles-destinos.summary: Save combinations of destinations, title and category, and apply them with one click. Up to 6 profiles.
perfiles-destinos.metaDescription: How to save combinations of enabled destinations and apply them with one click, without touching each toggle by hand.
perfiles-destinos.content:
A profile saves a combination of enabled destinations under a name. One click applies that profile: it turns those destinations on, turns the rest off — it doesn't "add", it replaces.

Create a profile

  1. Turn destinations on and off the way you want them.
  2. Press "Save current".
  3. Give it a name (e.g. "Twitch only" or "Everything").
012

Delete a profile

Tap the ✕ on the profile's chip. Limit: 6 saved profiles.

If you delete a destination a profile used, the profile keeps working with the rest of the destinations it had saved.

From the Stream Deck

A profile can also be assigned to a physical Stream Deck button.

Title and category per profile

Each profile also remembers the stream title and the category/game. One button to switch from "just chatting" to "ranked" — destinations, title and game all change together. One click applies the profile AND updates the title/category on the connected platforms (via OAuth).

3
highlights: A profile saves a combination of active destinations under a name.
Applying a profile replaces the current setup, it doesn't add to it.
Up to 6 profiles, also assignable to a Stream Deck button.

Schedule start

Pick a future time for the selected destinations to start on their own, without needing to be there at the exact moment.

  1. Open "Schedule start" in the panel.
  2. Choose the destinations and the time.
  3. Confirm with "Schedule".
01

Pre-flight check

"Check before going live" button — runs a quick check before starting, useful to avoid going live with something misconfigured. It's in the same actions panel as "Schedule start".

23
highlights: Schedule a future time for destinations to start on their own.
"Pre-flight check" verifies everything's fine before going live.
Both options live in the same actions panel.

resumen-stream.title: Stream summary
resumen-stream.summary: Duration, peak viewers, chat messages and average bitrate when you finish streaming, plus your session history.
resumen-stream.metaDescription: The automatic summary Muxlyve builds when a stream ends: duration, viewers, chat and bitrate.
resumen-stream.content:
When a stream ends, Muxlyve builds an automatic summary with:

  • Total duration.
  • Peak viewers per platform.
  • Number of chat messages received.
  • Average bitrate per destination.
0

Session history

Every time you actually go live, Muxlyve saves an automatic record: date, duration, platforms used and peak viewers. Your own stream history, without depending on each platform's separate analytics.

100% local — no account or cloud needed — and it keeps the last 100 sessions.

1
highlights: Automatic summary when you finish: duration, viewer peaks, chat, bitrate.
Local history of the last 100 sessions, no account or cloud.

control-lan.title: Control Muxlyve from another machine on your network
control-lan.summary: Control destinations, chat and Stream Deck from a machine other than the one streaming.
control-lan.metaDescription: How to control destinations, chat and Stream Deck from another machine on your network, with secure remote access.
control-lan.content:
Use case: you use a secondary computer to stream, with Muxlyve receiving the signal from your main PC running OBS — you can control Muxlyve from your main PC without any issue.

Turn on "Allow Stream Deck / chat from another machine" in Preferences. The connection uses an access token — only a device with that token can control your instance.

01

Related: Show chat on your stream and Stream Deck plugin.
highlights: Control Muxlyve from another machine on your network with an access token.
Useful to separate the streaming PC from the one controlling destinations and chat.

exportar-importar-config.title: Export and import your configuration
exportar-importar-config.summary: Back up destinations and settings to a password-encrypted .mux file, to restore on another machine.
exportar-importar-config.metaDescription: How to back up your configuration into a password-protected, encrypted .mux file, and restore it on another machine.
exportar-importar-config.content:
Switched PCs, reinstalled, or helping someone else end up with the exact same setup as you — without rewriting every destination and setting by hand. From Preferences → System, Muxlyve packages destinations, webhooks and the rest of your settings into a single password-encrypted .mux file.

012

Export

Press "Export", choose a password to protect the file, and save it wherever you want. Everything's inside: destinations, webhooks, profiles and the rest of your settings, encrypted with that password.

Import

Press "Import", select the .mux file and enter the password it was exported with. If the file comes from a different account than the one currently active, Muxlyve warns before applying anything — it never silently overwrites someone else's configuration.
highlights: Full backup (destinations, webhooks, profiles) in an encrypted .mux file.
Protected with a password you choose.
Muxlyve warns before overwriting another account's configuration.

avisos-discord-telegram.title: Discord and Telegram alerts when you go live (and end)
avisos-discord-telegram.summary: Automatic message to up to 3 Discord webhooks and 3 Telegram bots when you start and end your stream.
avisos-discord-telegram.metaDescription: How to configure Discord webhooks and Telegram bots so Muxlyve automatically alerts when you start and finish your stream.
avisos-discord-telegram.content:
Muxlyve sends an automatic message when you go live AND when you finish streaming, to up to 3 Discord webhooks and 3 Telegram bots at once — your community finds out about the start and the end, without you having to write it yourself every time.

0

Discord

  1. In Discord: Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
  2. Copy the webhook URL.
  3. Paste it into Muxlyve, in Preferences → Webhooks.
  4. Tap "Test" to confirm it works before going live.

Telegram

Create the bot with BotFather

  1. Look up @BotFather on Telegram (the official bot for creating bots) and open a chat with it.
  2. Type /newbot.
  3. Choose a display name, then a username ending in "bot" (e.g. my_channel_alerts_bot) — BotFather warns if it's already taken.
  4. BotFather replies with the token — a long line like 123456789:AAHqhK9DsSNGCQnQanCwHzXTVo1TVe0MYCA. That's the one that goes in Muxlyve. If you lose it: in BotFather, /mybots → pick the bot → "API Token" → "Revoke current token" generates a new one.
1

Getting the chat ID — the method depends on group vs. channel

If it's a group (or supergroup):

  1. Add @RawDataBot (or @getidsbot) to the group like any other member.
  2. As soon as it joins, it drops a message with all the chat data — look for "id" there (it starts with a minus sign, e.g. -1001234567890).
  3. Copy that number, remove the bot from the group if you won't use it there anymore.
2

If it's a channel: channels work differently — a bot added as a plain member can't see or post anything there, so the group method doesn't work on a channel. Two ways to get the ID anyway:

  1. Forward a message (the simplest, no need to add any bot to the channel): forward any message FROM the channel, privately, to @JsonDumpBot or @RawDataBot. It replies with the full JSON — look for forward_from_chat → id: -100.... That's the ID.
3
  • With the bot itself: in the channel → Administrators → add the bot as an administrator (not as a member — as a member it's not enough). Post something, then open https://api.telegram.org/botTOKEN/getUpdates (replacing TOKEN with the real token) and look for channel_post → chat → id: -100....

    • The invite link (t.me/+AbCdEfGh...) does NOT work as a chat ID — it's just a link to join, it doesn't identify the channel to the API.

    Shortcut if the group/channel is public (has an @username): use @channel_username directly in Muxlyve's Chat ID field, no need to look up any number.

    Group, supergroup and channel IDs always start with -100 when numeric — if the number doesn't start that way, it's probably a person's ID, not a group's or channel's.

    Saving it in Muxlyve

    1. Paste the token and the chat ID into Muxlyve.
    2. Tap "Save" — unlike Discord, Telegram requires an explicit save because the bot needs the token and the chat ID together.

    Editing the message

    There's a dedicated button on the main screen (icon next to "Schedule start") to edit the alert message. It's the same text for both platforms: Discord understands bold, italics and links; Telegram shows it as plain text.

    From that same modal, "Test" sends the saved message to every configured channel at once.

    45

    On start and on finish

    The "Alert message" modal has separate tabs — On start / On finish — each with its own text and its own cooldown. The closing alert only gets sent if a stream actually happened (never a closing alert without an opening one).

    6
highlights: Automatic message when you go live AND when you finish.
Up to 3 Discord webhooks and 3 Telegram bots at once.
The Telegram bot is created through BotFather.

audio-cortado.title: Dead audio alert
audio-cortado.summary: Native notification if it doesn't detect real audio for 20 seconds while you're live.
audio-cortado.metaDescription: Muxlyve warns you with a native notification if it doesn't detect real audio for 20 seconds while you're live.
audio-cortado.content:
Disconnected microphone, capture app crashed — you find out right away, not when someone tells you in chat 20 minutes later.

If Muxlyve doesn't detect real audio for 20 seconds while you're live, it sends a native system notification. It measures the actual input signal, so it doesn't trigger on a normal pause.

0

It can be disabled from Preferences, for anyone who'd rather not get this alert.
highlights: Native notification if it doesn't detect real audio for 20 seconds while live.
Can be disabled from Preferences.

preguntas-frecuentes.title: Frequently asked questions
preguntas-frecuentes.summary: Internet, TikTok, compatibility with other encoders, quality and reporting bugs.
preguntas-frecuentes.metaDescription: Internet, TikTok reconnection, compatibility with other encoders, signal quality, bitrate limit, notifications, Linux and how to report a bug.
preguntas-frecuentes.content:
Do I need internet just to stream, or also to use the app?

Activating the license does need internet, once. Streaming doesn't depend on Muxlyve's cloud — the signal is forwarded directly from your machine to each platform.

Why does TikTok ask to reconnect the key so often?

It's a limitation of TikTok's platform, not Muxlyve's: the stream key TikTok issues regenerates every ~2 hours.

Does it work with vMix, N.Air or any other encoder?

Yes. Muxlyve isn't an OBS plugin — it receives any RTMP signal, wherever it comes from.

Does my stream quality drop from forwarding to 4 platforms?

No. Muxlyve uses -c copy: it forwards the signal without re-encoding, with minimal CPU load.

Can I set a bitrate limit on a destination?

Yes, it's optional. On each destination's card you can expand "Max bitrate (kbps) — optional" and set a cap. As long as your actual bitrate stays below it, Muxlyve keeps forwarding without re-encoding. Only if it stays above the limit does it re-encode that specific destination to bring it down to the cap. With no limit set, it never re-encodes.

Does it warn me if a destination drops while I'm doing something else?

Yes. If you have another window or a game in the foreground and a destination drops, Muxlyve sends a native operating-system notification (not an in-app alert). On some Linux distros without a notification daemon this may not be available — it fails silently, it doesn't break the app.

Does Muxlyve run on Linux?

Today the app is available for Windows and macOS. Linux is on the roadmap, but not confirmed yet.

Where do I report a bug?

"Report an issue" button inside the app — it attaches the logs automatically. If you'd rather not use that, write to us directly at soporte@muxlyve.com.
